prompt: Complete BinaryRecordCodec so encode writes a PlayerStat with DataOutputStream (writeUTF, writeInt, writeDouble, writeBoolean) and decode reads the same values back in the same order.
explanation: DataOutputStream and DataInputStream are a matched pair that write and read Java primitives in a fixed big-endian layout, so the only contract between writer and reader is the ORDER of the calls -- there are no field names in the stream. writeUTF adds a two-byte length prefix so a variable-length String can be found again, which is why the encoded size is predictable. Read the values in a different order and you get silent garbage rather than an error, which is the main hazard of hand-rolled binary formats.
hints: encode needs a ByteArrayOutputStream underneath the DataOutputStream; return its toByteArray() after the stream is closed.
decode mirrors encode exactly: readUTF, readInt, readDouble, readBoolean, in that order.
A record's components are read with method calls: stat.name(), stat.level(), and so on.
